rich_summary: After Bhishma’s fall in the Kurukshetra war, the Kaurava army sinks into despair and calls desperately for Karna, their long‑withheld champion. Sanjaya recounts how Karna had refused to fight while Bhishma commanded, angered after being publicly classified by Bhishma as only an “Ardha‑ratha.” With Bhishma gone, the Kauravas now look to Karna as their last great hope, like men seeking a boat to cross a dangerous river. Dhritarashtra anxiously wonders whether Karna can fill the immense void left by Bhishma. When Karna arrives, he mourns Bhishma’s greatness, reflects on the transience of life and power, and then steels himself to defend the Kuru host. Accepting the burden of leadership, he vows to confront the Pandavas and win immortal fame or die in battle.

highlight_spans.why: The opening word captures the emotional state of the Kaurava army after Bhishma’s fall.
The desperate cry for Karna signals the army’s shift of hope from Bhishma to Karna.

top_scenes.scene_text: The Kaurava kings on the battlefield crying out 'Karna! Karna!' amid the gloom after Bhishma’s fall.
Karna arriving on the battlefield with tearful eyes as Bhishma lies fallen, while the Kaurava army looks to him for salvation.
